newsitem.title: USA: US Mid-Atlantic spot power up amid short-covering.
newsitem.headline: US Mid-Atlantic spot power up amid short-covering.

text.p: Physical electricity prices in the U.S. Mid-Atlantic region rose Monday amid keen buying interests by participants which were short of energy to meet Tuesday's expected demand.
"People were getting caught short-covering. Next-day prices were higher," said one power marketer.

In the Pennsylvania-New Jersey-Maryland (PJM) Interconnect pool, electricity for outer-month delivery was bolstered by firm fuel oil and natural gas prices in the region, albeit very few units have been consuming either fuel for electric generation, brokers and traders said.
"People are getting nervous...about fuel oil and gas prices coming up," the marketer added.

This week's scheduled returns of the 1,100 megawatt (MW) Peach Bottom 2 nuclear unit in Delta, Pa., and 833 MW Beaver Valley 2 nuclear unit in Shippingport, Pa., from refueling were not major concerns in today's trading, traders said.
Firm electricity prices for heavy load periods on Tuesday were quoted at $22.00-$23.00 per megawatt hour (MWh), up from Friday's $19.50-$20.50 range for Monday power.
PJM firm, peak power for the rest of the week and October was assessed at $20.50-$21.00, higher than Friday's $20.00-$20.50.
November PJM was valued at $22.65-$22.85, above a quote of $22.35-$22.55 on Friday.
December PJM was discussed at $26.70-$26.80, up slightly from Friday's $26.60-$26.70.
PJM electricity for the balance of the 1996 fourth quarter was pegged at $22.85-$23.35, higher than Friday's range of $22.75-$23.25.
PJM firm, peak power for January/February 1997 delivery was assessed at $30.25-$30.45, up from a quote of $29.90-$30.25 on Friday.
First-quarter 1997 PJM electricity was valued at $28.10-$28.60, up from Friday's $27.75-$28.25, and second-quarter 1997 PJM was quoted at $21.85-$22.85, higher than Friday's $21.50-$22.20.
